title: The lead agent's plan is kept whole and shown back to it
request: The owner's goal for the Hierarchical Planning work is a better plan for the person: understand the problem, break it down, plan, carry it out in order. The think-first measurement had shown a gain on people the builder had not tuned on and a loss on two people.
spec: Behind the think-first switch only: the plan's numbered steps and its closing lines are never cut by the word limit; the plan is kept in the case's state and shown back to the model on later turns; the prompt asks for the ways to solve the problem weighed against each other, as many steps as the work needs, and a line on when to stop and one on what to do if a step fails.
plan: read the two conversations where the switch made the plan worse
take the plan out of the message before the word limit is applied to the rest
keep the plan in the state and its checkpoint, and show it back on the next turn
more room for the first full message's reply, so it does not come back empty
measure on the known people against the same model alone, then the held-out people once

decisions.decision: The plan is read from the message by code, not written through a tool
decisions.why: the model's tool calls came back malformed several times in eight conversations; numbered lines are easy to read

decisions.decision: The plan lives in the agent's state first, not in the core case file
decisions.why: a frozen contract should change only after a measurement shows the plan helps

decisions.decision: A clear, simple request gets short first parts and the plan in full
decisions.why: on a clear request the part on what needs care grew and squeezed the plan

decisions.decision: Everything is behind the think-first switch
decisions.why: the switch is off until its gate passes on the held-out people

change: A reader of the plan block in a message, the word limit applied around it, the plan kept in the state and its checkpoint and shown back as a note, a larger reply limit for the first full message, and the think-first prompt's points on options and the plan.

findings.defect: With the think-first switch on, the word limit cut the plan first.
findings.scenario: The plan is the last part of the first full message; for a clear request the part on what needs care took most of the room and the plan that reached the person was shorter than without the switch.
findings.cause: the message is cut from its end and the plan is at its end
findings.fix: The plan is taken out before the limit is applied and is put back whole.

findings.defect: Three of sixteen first replies came back empty or cut with the switch on.
findings.scenario: A first full message with its plan, written after the model's own thinking, passed the reply limit of a step.
findings.cause: the reply limit of a step was set for short replies
findings.fix: With the switch on a step's reply limit is twice as large.

findings.defect: Nothing made the agent follow the plan it had written.
findings.scenario: On the next turn the model saw the case file and the conversation, and wrote a new plan or none.
findings.cause: the plan existed only as prose in an earlier message
findings.fix: The plan is shown back on later turns with the instruction to keep to it and to say which step it is on.

outcome: The change is in place behind the switch and its tests pass; it has not been measured on a live model yet.
lessons: A limit that cuts from the end cuts whatever was put last, and the plan was put last.
Read the conversations behind a lower score before changing a prompt.
risks: A reply with two numbered lists may have the wrong one taken as the plan.
A plan shown back every turn may make the agent hold to a plan that new facts made wrong; the note allows a change with its reason.
